575.english_source:
575 — ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal reported:
I asked Anas ibn Mālik may Allah be pleased with him:
“Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declare Madinah a sanctuary?”
He replied:
“Yes.
‘The area between such-and-such and such-and-such is sacred. Its trees are not to be cut. Whoever introduces an offense within it, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7306) and Muslim (1366).
The wording above is that of al-Bukhārī.
Muslim adds:
“Allah will accept from him on the Day of Resurrection neither ṣarf (voluntary deeds) nor ʿadl (obligatory deeds).”

575.full_source_content:
٥٧٥ — عن عاصم الأحول قال:
قلت لأنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه:
أحرَّم رسول الله ﷺ المدينة؟
قال:
نعم.
«ما بين كذا إلى كذا، لا يُقطع شجرها. من أحدث فيها حدثاً، فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٣٠٦)، ومسلم (١٣٦٦).
واللفظ للبخاري.
وزاد مسلم:
«لا يقبل الله منه يوم القيامة صرفاً ولا عدلاً».

576.english_source:
576 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib may Allah be pleased with him said:
“We possess nothing except the Book of Allah and this written sheet from the Prophet ﷺ:
‘Madinah is sacred from ʿĀʾir (a mountain marking one boundary of Madinah’s sanctuary) to such-and-such. Whoever introduces an offense within it or shelters an offender, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people…’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Ḥajj (1870) and Muslim in al-Ḥajj (1370), with the wording of al-Bukhārī.

577.english_source:

“Madinah is a sanctuary. Whoever introduces an offense within it or shelters an offender, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people; and on the Day of Resurrection neither ʿadl (obligatory deeds) nor ṣarf (voluntary deeds) will be accepted from him.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (1371).

594.english_source:
594 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb may Allah be pleased with him reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When Adam died, the angels washed him with water an odd number of times, prepared a laḥd grave for him (a grave with a side niche dug into the qiblah-facing wall), and said:
‘This is the practice of Adam for his descendants.’”
Ḥasan: Narrated by al-Ḥākim (2/545).

646.english_source:
646 — Abū Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him reported:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“Whoever spends a pair of something (two items of the same kind) in the path of Allah will be called by the keepers of Paradise:
‘O so-and-so, come!’”
Abū Bakr may Allah be pleased with him asked:
“Such a person will have no cause for loss?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“I hope that you will be among them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3216) and Muslim (1027:86).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢١٦)، ومسلم (١٠٢٧: ٨٦).

662.english_source:
662 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them said:
“The Qurʾān was sent down all at once from al-Dhikr (the Preserved Tablet) on the twenty-fourth night of Ramaḍān and was placed in Bayt al-ʿIzzah (a place in the lowest heaven).”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (7991), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (12381), al-Ḥākim (2/223), and Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (3/189).
In another narration:
“Then Jibrīl began descending with it to the Prophet ﷺ, reciting it in measured recitation.”

صحيح: رواه النسائي في الكبرى (٧٩٩١)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٢٣٨١)، والحاكم (٢/٢٢٣)، وابن جرير الطبري في تفسيره (٣/١٨٩).
وفي رواية:
«فجعل جبريل ينزل على النبي ﷺ ويرتله ترتيلاً».

665.english_source:
665 — Ibn ʿAbbās may Allah be pleased with them said concerning the statement of Allah Most High:
“Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree.”
[Sūrat al-Qadr 97:1]
“The Qurʾān was sent down all at once on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven. Thereafter, it descended according to the positions of the stars (that is, in successive portions at intervals, one part after another), and Allah would send portions of it down to His Messenger one after another.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Ibn Jarīr in his Tafsīr (24/543) and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11689).

701.arabic_source:
٧٠١ — عن عائشة، وعن أنس رضي الله عنهم:
«أن النبي ﷺ مرَّ بقومٍ يُلقِّحون، فقال:
لو لم تفعلوا لصلح.
قال: فخرج شيصًا، فمرَّ بهم فقال:
ما لنخلكم؟
قالوا: قلت كذا وكذا.
قال:
أنتم أعلم بأمر دنياكم».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٣٦٣).
وقوله:
«خرج شيصًا»
هو البُسر الرديء الذي إذا يبس صار حشفًا.
خلاصة القول في عصمة الأنبياء

701.english_source:
701 — ʿĀʾishah and Anas may Allah be pleased with them reported:
The Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were pollinating their date-palms and said:
“Perhaps if you did not do it, they would turn out well.”
But the fruit came out as shīṣ. He later passed by them and asked:
“What happened to your date-palms?”
They replied:
“You said such-and-such.”
He said:
“You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your worldly life.”
Ṣaḥīḥ: Narrated by Muslim (2363).
The expression:
“It came out as shīṣ”
means poor-quality dates which, when they dry, become shriveled and worthless.
A Summary Concerning the Infallibility of the Prophets
Ahl al-Sunnah and the majority of Muslims agree that the Prophets, peace be upon them, are protected from error in what they convey from Allah Most High and in delivering His message, because this protection fulfills the purpose of revelation and prophethood.
Ahl al-Sunnah also hold that minor sins, as opposed to major sins, may occur from them in their actions
(More precisely: this is the position of the majority of Muslim scholars. Ibn Taymiyyah attributes it to the majority of scholars and specifically states that it was the view of most scholars of tafsīr, ḥadīth, and fiqh; he also reports from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Āmidī that it was the position of most Ashʿarīs. He further explains that the Prophets, peace be upon them, are not left to persist in such minor sins, but repent from them and are corrected by Allah. See: Ibn Taymiyyah, Majmūʿ al-Fatāwā, vol. 4, pp. 319–320. However, a number of Sunni scholars held that the Prophets are protected from minor sins as well. Among those associated with this stricter position are Abū Isḥāq al-Isfarāyīnī, Ibn Fūrak, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, and Tāj al-Dīn al-Subkī. Al-Shawkānī records this disagreement in Irshād al-Fuḥūl, vol. 1, p. 136, and Tāj al-Dīn al-Subkī states in Jamʿ al-Jawāmiʿ the position that the Prophets are protected even from minor sins. Therefore, this is a recognized area of disagreement among Sunni scholars, and neither position should be presented as an absolute consensus.)
based on what has been reported in the Qurʾān and authentic narrations. However, they do not persist in them; rather, they hasten to repentance and seeking forgiveness. Thus, they are protected from persisting in such acts, and their repentance itself is an example to be followed, since we have been commanded to take them as models. And success is from Allah.

746.arabic_source:
٧٤٦ — عن أبي عبد الرحمن الجهني رضي الله عنه قال:
بينا نحن عند رسول الله ﷺ طلع ركبان، فلما رآهما قال:
«كنديان مذحجيان».
حتى أتياه، فإذا رجلان من مذحج.
قال:
فدنا إليه أحدهما ليبايعه، فأخذ بيده، فقال:
يا رسول الله، أرأيت من رآك فآمن بك وصدقك واتبعك، ماذا له؟
قال:
«طوبى له» (أي: الخيرُ العظيمُ والسعادةُ والنعيمُ له. وقد قال النبي ﷺ: «طُوبَى لِمَن رآني وآمنَ بي، ثم طُوبَى ثم طُوبَى ثم طُوبَى لِمَن آمنَ بي ولم يرني». فقيل له: وما طُوبَى؟ قال: «شجرةٌ في الجنةِ مسيرةُ مائةِ عامٍ، ثيابُ أهلِ الجنةِ تخرجُ من أكمامِها». رواه أحمد (١١٦٧٣)، وأبو يعلى (١٣٧٤)، وابن حبان (٧٤١٣). وقال ابن حجر العسقلاني: «حديث حسن» — الأمالي المطلقة، ص ٤٧، رقم ٨٤.).
قال:
فمسح على يده فانصرف.
ثم أقبل الآخر حتى أخذ بيده ليبايعه، فقال:
يا رسول الله، أرأيت من آمن بك وصدقك واتبعك ولم يرك؟
قال:
«طوبى له، ثم طوبى له، ثم طوبى له».
قال:
فمسح على يده فانصرف.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٣٨٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٢/٢٨٩)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٢٧٦٩).

While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, two riders appeared.
When he saw them, he said:
“Two men from Kindah, from Madhḥij.”
When they reached him, they turned out to be two men from Madhḥij.
One of them came forward to pledge allegiance to him. The Prophet ﷺ took his hand, and the man asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about one who saw you, believed in you, affirmed you, and followed you? What will he receive?”
He replied:
“Ṭūbā for him” (i.e., abundant goodness, happiness, and bliss for him. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Ṭūbā for the one who saw me and believed in me, and Ṭūbā, then Ṭūbā, then Ṭūbā for the one who believed in me without seeing me.” He was asked, “What is Ṭūbā?” He replied: “A tree in Paradise, [the extent of] a hundred years’ journey; the garments of the people of Paradise come forth from its coverings.” Narrated by Aḥmad (11673), Abū Yaʿlā (1374), and Ibn Ḥibbān (7413). He then passed his hand over the man’s hand, and the man departed.
The other man then came forward and took his hand to pledge allegiance.
He asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what about one who believes in you, affirms you, and follows you but never sees you?”
He replied:
“Ṭūbā for him, then Ṭūbā for him, then Ṭūbā for him.”
He then passed his hand over his hand, and the man departed.
